claims.text: The reported initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of about 423 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
Approximately 0.5 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles should be introduced during mechanical alloying before spark plasma sintering.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can consolidate a refractory high-entropy alloy containing a BCC matrix and oxide precipitates.
The proposed processing route will produce a uniform distribution of approximately 20 nm Y2O3 particles in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
Dispersed oxide particles can contribute precipitation strengthening in a refractory BCC high-entropy alloy.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin dislocations and inhibit their motion in TiVNbTa.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries and limit grain-boundary sliding in TiVNbTa.
The nanoparticle dispersion will suppress recovery and grain coarsening at high temperature.
Suppressing dislocation mobility, recovery, and grain coarsening will reduce creep and thermal softening.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering improved the strength of equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi through grain refinement and TiO precipitation strengthening.
At 1273 K, Y2O3-modified TiVNbTa will have a yield strength above approximately 450 MPa.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will retain acceptable ductility while its elevated-temperature strength increases.
Testing from room temperature to 1273 K and deformation to 30–40% strain represents service conditions for a W/CuCrZr intermediate heat-transfer layer.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on obtaining a uniform Y2O3 dispersion and may vary with milling and sintering conditions.
The intervention can be tested against an undoped TiVNbTa control processed under identical spark plasma sintering conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength increase exceeding about 100 MPa at 1273 K is proposed as a falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: The predicted target is above approximately 450 MPa from a 330 MPa baseline, implying an increase of roughly 120 MPa, whereas the falsification rule separately uses an example threshold of greater than 100 MPa. These thresholds are close but not identical, leaving ambiguous whether a 101–119 MPa increase confirms the stated target.
